data.summary: The application completes its startup in approximately 6 seconds, but the pod remains unready for 65 seconds due to an overly conservative initialDelaySeconds of 45 seconds in the readiness probe. The subsequent polling interval further delays the transition to the Ready state, causing a significant breach of the 10-second SLO.

findings.statement: The application reports startup completion at 6.069s, well within the 10s SLO.
The readiness probe is configured with an initialDelaySeconds of 45s and a periodSeconds of 20s, which forces the pod to wait significantly longer than the actual application startup time.
The total time spent in the readiness phase is 58.931s, which accounts for the majority of the 65.0s total startup duration.

ruled_out.reason: The image pull duration was only 4.141s for 53MB, indicating normal pull performance.
Application initialisation was fast, taking only 0.928s.
Scheduling was instantaneous at 0.0s, indicating no resource or scheduling constraints.

recommendations.action: Reduce initialDelaySeconds in the readiness probe
recommendations.rationale: The current 45s delay is significantly higher than the observed 6s startup time, unnecessarily delaying pod readiness.
A startup probe would allow the application to signal readiness as soon as it is ready, while still protecting against slow-starting instances.
